diagrams.title: The Consignment Broker Workflow
diagrams.subtitle: Never own the iron; earn 5% to 12% on someone else's machine

stages.label: Call the seller for the story
stages.detail: Find out why the machine is on the market, whether a fire, worn-out iron, or a job that ran out, before money moves.

stages.label: Price on condition, not seller hope
stages.detail: Overpriced units die because people do not pay more than something is worth.

stages.label: Publish sharp photos and full descriptions
stages.detail: Weak photos and thin descriptions cut leads, offers, and final price.

stages.label: Push one listing to several channels
stages.detail: Dealer software sends a single listing out to multiple sales channels at once.

stages.label: Screen buyers and close remotely
stages.detail: Shield the seller from tire kickers and call only when a buyer is serious; the Academy teaches selling over 50% of equipment sight unseen.

diagrams.caption: Retail commissions run $2,700 to $4,500 per sale, and the average consignor brings 3.5 machines, so one client can feed retail, wholesale, and auction revenue.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Sequence assembled from separate practitioner tips; the speakers did not publish it as one ordered workflow. Commission band of 5% to 12% per Equipment Broker Academy. Sellers also report machines sitting 105 days to six months.
diagrams.note: Sources - Noah Graff (Swarfcast), Charles Petrov (Equipment Broker Academy), Duncan (ResaleWeekly), Pav Jam, Machinery Manager, and a Boom & Bucket seller account.

stages.detail: Caterpillar excavator package for an excavation contractor.

stages.detail: Michael Chen, a student with zero finance background, arranged financing without lending his own money.

stages.conversion: Above it, request the last three years of tax returns or audited financials
stages.detail: Signed proposal plus one monthly payment as a performance deposit before any credit app goes to a lender.

stages.label: Broker spread on the $350,000 package
stages.detail: One approval on the excavator package.

stages.label: First-deal commission
stages.conversion: Academy range of $2,000 to $5,000 per funded deal

diagrams.caption: Commission claims run wide, from $2,000 to $5,000 per funded deal up to Jermane Cheathem's claim of 20 points on a $100,000 deal.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Stages mix two separate practitioner examples ($350,000 and $180,000 excavators) plus the credit-app ceiling; they are not one tracked deal. Application-only ceilings reported from $75,000 to $350,000; credit floors from 580 to 650.
diagrams.note: Sources - Equipment Finance Academy, Buzz Glover (BizLoanConsultants.com), and Jermane Cheathem.

diagrams.title: Winning Below the Comps
diagrams.subtitle: A 2023 Cascadia bought online at Ritchie Bros.
diagrams.caption: The 572,000 km unit closed at $76,000 against comps of $85k, $82k, and $81k, while a favored 361k-km unit ran to $102k and was abandoned.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Bid Agent valued the unit at $86k to $87k; the top of that range is the starting bar. Bar gaps are arithmetic between reported figures. Buyer's premiums of 12-19%, a 10% auction fee plus 13% HST, and a 3-4% card surcharge sit outside this hammer comparison.
diagrams.note: Source - Ronin of ET Transport, using the Bid Agent Chrome extension and a $500,000 Ritchie credit line; the buyer claimed '$10,000' made.

diagrams.title: Reading Used-Equipment Price Points
diagrams.subtitle: Reported auction swings, stalls, and prep spend
diagrams.unit: Dollars as quoted (Steiger figure in Canadian dollars)

bars.label: Farm Journal tracked model, average to high
Cab interior refresh spend
bars.display: $7 rattle can vs. roughly $200 interior kit

diagrams.caption: Supply drives the read: five-year-old high-horse tractor listings fell 79%, and auctions rose 19.5% while 1-3 year old units sold fell 19.9%.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Each bar is a separate practitioner-reported figure, not a common index. A stalled bid is not a ceiling; documented work orders and warranty history add value buyers pay for.
diagrams.note: Sources - Machinery Pete, Farm Journal, RealAgriculture, Luke Fritshaw of Ritchie Bros., and Patrick Shivers.

diagrams.title: Lien and Fraud Gates Before the Iron Moves
diagrams.subtitle: Prove the machine is not already pledged, then prove the money

nodes.question: Does a Secretary of State UCC search on the debtor's exact legal name come back clean?
nodes.fail_action: Order the $15 Texas plain copy to read the collateral description; have the dealer pay the lender directly, as in $8,000 to the lender and $2,000 to the seller on $10,000.

nodes.question: Does a separate search under the secured party's name clear blanket liens?
nodes.fail_action: Never clear collateral on a UCC-3 termination alone; verify the underlying debt is satisfied.

nodes.question: Does the hull, motor, trailer, or machine carry a readable serial, HIN, or VIN?
nodes.fail_action: Walk away; it could be stolen product.

nodes.question: Is payment a verified wire, with no cashier's check and no stand-in collector for an out-of-state buyer?
nodes.fail_action: Stop the release; verify any changed wiring instructions by calling a number already held, never one from the email.

diagrams.caption: A buyer who takes a liened machine can lose it to the original lender; a misspelled debtor name can hide a million-dollar lien.
diagrams.assumptions_note: UCC filings generally stay active for five years. New York search fee is $25 by credit card; copies require check or money order. Gate order assembled from separate practitioner rules.
diagrams.note: Sources - Garden Shop Pro, NerdWallet Small Business, CSC, OnWaterTVAustralia, Boom & Bucket, Living in Fort Myers, and jesseleblancatlanta.

diagrams.title: Imaging and Data-Center Equipment Broker Hub
diagrams.subtitle: Buy as the facility exits, prove identity, resell whole or as parts

center.focus: Prove technical identity with tube scan seconds, software licenses, nameplates, battery date codes, and acceptance test reports.

spokes.kpi: Year, make, model, tube age, licensed software, and gantry photos front, back, and side before pricing
40 to 50% below new with a one-year all-inclusive warranty baseline; ISO 13485 certified
$12,000 paid to owner, room cleared in 10 days; generator load bank tested before resale

diagrams.caption: Block Imaging says new can cost up to twice the price of used or refurbished; Reclaim Atlas recovered removal cost through generator and UPS resale.
diagrams.assumptions_note: MRI savings combine a 210 purchase gap (805 OEM vs. 595 MXR) with post-warranty service at $85,000 instead of $110,000 per year. Oak Ridge teardown covered a 225 kVA UPS and a 180 kW standby generator.
diagrams.note: Sources - MXR Imaging, Block Imaging, Reclaim Atlas, Probo Medical UK, and Keentel Engineering.

diagrams.title: Undercarriage Wear Thresholds
diagrams.subtitle: Measure component by component, never accept a seller's percentage
diagrams.total_range: 31% measured wear to a 60% pin and bush turn point

buckets.label: Measured Komatsu wear at 4,700 hours
buckets.notes: 1,010 of 3,200 points on a 2010 Komatsu excavator.

buckets.label: Price as needing undercarriage soon
buckets.notes: Wear accelerates past this band; not half its life left.

buckets.label: Pin and bush turn trigger
buckets.notes: Turn at 7,000 hours or 60% wear on the rails.

diagrams.caption: Undercarriage replacement runs 12,000 to upwards of 70 grand, so pumped-tight tracks, cut links, and welded adjusters get checked before bidding.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Percentages are wear unless labeled remaining. Oil samples cost less than 10 dollars typical, less than 20 on the high side, with 24 to 48 hour turnaround; Carter recommends sampling every 250 hours.
diagrams.note: Sources - C&C Equipment, Hunter Valley Tracks, Volvo Construction Equipment - North America, Shelly Eckert of Chevron via EquipmentWorld, and Carter Machinery.

diagrams.title: Adjacent Equipment Plays Roadmap
diagrams.subtitle: Buy or broker what the market mislabeled; own the buyer network

weeks.title: Source surplus iron
weeks.deliverable: Bid list with demil codes read first; DEMIL A and Q transfer intact, and some Code H dozer fixes start with a $10 filter.
weeks.gate: Data plate matched to the DLA catalog; milky fluids, pin bosses, and grouser height checked.

weeks.title: Source salvage units
weeks.deliverable: Underwater units bought from insurers and salvagedsale.com; one flood machine has run about 2,000 hours since.

weeks.title: Structure the auction or consignment
weeks.deliverable: 6% seller fee plus 10% buyer premium, $3,200 on a $20K machine; seller proceeds never touch the operating account.
weeks.gate: No net guarantee without reserves; $620K in comps produced a $375K sale and a $150K hit.

weeks.title: Exit through export or parts
weeks.deliverable: Excavators shipped only on 50/50 terms; a $1,500 F-150 parted out for $4,000.
weeks.gate: Verified buyer and purchase order locked; galamsey buyers refused.

diagrams.caption: Plain Finance reports $500K in year three from its auction house; Jermane Cheathem reports $50M+ in brokered equipment deals.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Week grouping is an organizing sequence; practitioners did not report weekly timing. F-150 operating profit of about $1,400 is net of $150 tow, $600 labor, and $350 other costs.
diagrams.note: Sources - EquipmentWorld, Vantor Surplus, Plain Finance, CapitalCode, SwiftBridge Trading LLP, and Jermane Cheathem.
